newsitem.title: DENMARK: Heineken set to sell canned ale in Denmark.
newsitem.headline: Heineken set to sell canned ale in Denmark.

text.p: Dutch brewery giant Heineken said on Wednesday it was poised to sell canned beer in Denmark if the Danish parliament voted to lift its ban on tinned ale.

"If the sale of canned beer is permitted in Denmark, it will obviously open up new possibilities for us in the Danish market," Heineken press officer Margritha Meiger told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"We will probably try and launch our canned beer in the retail market. We have sold beer in Denmark for the past five years or so, sales are rising all the time but are still modest," she said.
Heineken is one of the biggest competitors of Danish brewer Carlsberg in international markets, but the Danish brewery group has around 82 percent of the domestic market.

Denmark, which operates a highly effective bottle deposit system, forbids beer in cans, a ban which recently drew severe criticism from Britain and France and which the European Commission says contravenes union competition rules.

Faced with a possible suit in the European Court, the Danish environment ministry is conducting a survey into the environmental effects of allowing beer cans in Denmark, but the report is not due for completion until the autumn.
On Wednesday, parliament was due to give a final reading to a bill allowing the import, production and use of beer cans using a deposit system.

The vote is expected to be close, with the ruling centre-left Social Democrat-led government coalition and left-wing opposition parties opposed to lifting the ban and the centre-right opposition in favour, parliamentary sources said.
